entities.summary:
Oliver von Paderborn, also known as Oliver Scholasticus or Oliver of Cologne, was a German cleric, crusader and chronicler. He was born in unknown year and died on September 18, 1227.

Born in unknown year in Germany, Oliver was destined for greatness, his family's influence and connections paving the way for his future.

He played a significant role in the Crusades as a preacher, participant and chronicler, his writings chronicling the events and experiences of the time.

Oliver's significance extends beyond his own lifetime, his contributions to the understanding and documentation of the Crusades leaving a lasting impact on the field of history.

As a cardinal-bishop of Sabina, Oliver was part of the inner circle of the Catholic Church, his influence extending beyond the borders of Europe.

He was the first Paderborn bishop to become a cardinal, a testament to his faith and dedication to his calling.

Oliver von Paderborn's legacy is complex and multifaceted, a reflection of the man himself.

In the annals of history, his name will be remembered for generations to come.

One striking statistic is that Oliver was one of the earliest chroniclers of the Fourth Crusade, his writings providing a unique window into the events of that tumultuous time.

'For God and the Holy Land', Oliver's mantra, encapsulates the essence of his being.
